title: Single phase incoming supply (up to 100 A)
summary: The parts of a single phase incoming supply up to 100 A, the types of overcurrent and earth leakage current, and the construction and protection features of a consumer unit.

sections.heading: Components of a single phase incoming supply
paragraphs: A typical single phase incoming supply has a distributor's cut-out (typically 80 A or 100 A), an electricity meter, meter tails and an electricity isolator switch. The isolator switch is not common on older installations.
Where an alternative energy supply such as solar PV is present, the installation also includes an isolator switch and RCD in the feed from the inverter, and connections from there to the main supply.
bullets: Distributor's cut-out: typically 80 A or 100 A.
Electricity meter.
Meter tails.
Electricity isolator switch (not common on older installations).

sections.heading: Distributor's cut-out and meter
paragraphs: The cut-out normally takes the form of a BS 88 cartridge fuse, commonly rated 80 A or 100 A. The carrier is removed by pulling it out, but it is protected by a seal. The seal is easily removed, but doing so can invoke heavy penalties if the electricity supplier discovers it.
Removing the fuse only breaks the line connection. The neutral connection will still be present.
The incoming supply connects directly to the meter from the cut-out. Like the cut-out, the meter is protected by a seal which should not be broken.
bullets: Cut-out: BS 88 cartridge fuse, commonly 80 A and 100 A.
Removing the fuse breaks the line only; the neutral remains connected.
Both the cut-out and the meter are sealed and the seals should not be broken.

sections.heading: Meter tails and the isolator switch
paragraphs: In theory the csa of the line and neutral tails would need to be calculated, but for supplies up to 100 A it is common to install 25 mm² conductors between the meter and the consumer unit. BS 7671 Table 4D1A (Reference Method B, because the tails between the fuse and the meter should be in trunking) gives a current carrying capacity of 101 A for 25 mm².
From the same table, a 16 mm² cable can carry up to 87 A where Reference Method C is used. This is why older installations with an 80 A fuse commonly had 16 mm² tails.
The isolator switch lets the main supply to the consumer unit be isolated and locked off when work is needed on that part of the circuit, for example when replacing the consumer unit.
bullets: Common tails for supplies up to 100 A: 25 mm² (101 A, Reference Method B).
16 mm² tails: up to 87 A (Reference Method C), common with older 80 A fuses.
Isolator switch: allows the supply to the consumer unit to be isolated and locked off.

sections.heading: Overcurrent and earth leakage current
paragraphs: Protective devices in a consumer unit must deal with both overcurrent and earth leakage current. BS 7671 Part 2 defines overcurrent as a current exceeding the rated value; for conductors the rated value is the current-carrying capacity. It is subdivided into overload current and fault current.

Overload current is an overcurrent in a circuit which is electrically sound, so the problem is caused by devices or equipment connected to the installation rather than the installation itself. Fault current is a current resulting from a fault, which may be in the installation (for example cable or equipment insulation failure) or in connected equipment (for example a motor short circuit).

Earth leakage current is called protective conductor current in BS 7671 Part 2: electric current appearing in a protective conductor, such as leakage current or current resulting from an insulation fault. It can be anything from a few milliamps to hundreds of amps, and the protective devices must deal with all conditions.
bullets: Overcurrent: a current exceeding the rated value.
Overload current: an overcurrent in an electrically sound circuit.
Fault current: a current resulting from a fault.

Short-circuit current: an overcurrent resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors having a difference in potential under normal operating conditions (zero Ω or very close to it).
Earth leakage current: current in the cpc resulting from a fault in the installation or connected equipment.

sections.heading: Consumer unit construction and protection
paragraphs: Double pole isolator switches are used to disconnect the supply to the distribution circuits. In a split supply consumer unit one circuit may have a manually operated double pole switch and the other a double pole isolator incorporating an RCD. The RCD protects against fault currents in any of the circuits it supplies.

Any fault before the circuit breakers that results in an overcurrent is protected by the 100 A distributor's cut-out, so all conductive components in the consumer unit up to the breakers must be rated at >100 A. A short circuit after a circuit breaker is protected by that circuit breaker, whose fault current rating (Icn) must be greater than the prospective fault current for that part of the circuit.
bullets: Double pole isolator switches disconnect the supply to the distribution circuits.
Components up to the breakers must be rated at >100 A.
Faults after a breaker are cleared by that circuit breaker.
Icn must be greater than the prospective fault current.

sections.heading: Basic protection and enclosure material
paragraphs: All external covers on a consumer unit must provide suitable protection against electric shock, meaning at least IP4X (BS 7671 416). All cable entry points must offer the same protection. With the covers removed for service work, all live parts must still be protected by suitable barriers or insulation. In the example unit, the cover over the main busbar forms a suitably labelled barrier.

Amendment 3 of BS 7671:2011 requires the enclosures of domestic consumer units and similar switchgear to be made of a non-combustible material or be enclosed within a non-combustible cabinet. Ferrous metal, such as steel, is an example of a non-combustible material.
bullets: External covers: at least IP4X, and cable entries the same.
Live parts must be protected by barriers or insulation when covers are removed.
Enclosure: non-combustible material or inside a non-combustible cabinet.
Steel (ferrous metal) is deemed non-combustible.

flashcards.front: What does a typical single phase incoming supply include?
flashcards.back: A distributor's cut-out (typically 80 A or 100 A), an electricity meter, meter tails and an electricity isolator switch (not common on older installations).

flashcards.front: What type of device is the distributor's cut-out, and what are its common ratings?
flashcards.back: A cartridge fuse of type BS 88, commonly rated 80 A and 100 A.

flashcards.front: What does removing the cut-out fuse disconnect?
flashcards.back: Only the line connection. The neutral connection is still present.

flashcards.front: What csa are meter tails commonly installed at for supplies up to 100 A?
flashcards.back: 25 mm². From BS 7671 Table 4D1A, Reference Method B, a 25 mm² cable has a current carrying capacity of 101 A.

flashcards.front: What is the electricity isolator switch for?
flashcards.back: It lets the main supply to the consumer unit be isolated and locked off, for example when replacing the consumer unit.
A current exceeding the rated value. For conductors the rated value is the current-carrying capacity. It is split into overload current and fault current.
An overcurrent occurring in a circuit which is electrically sound, caused by devices or equipment connected to the installation.
A current resulting from a fault, either in the installation (e.g. insulation failure) or in connected equipment (e.g. motor short circuit).

flashcards.front: What is earth leakage current called in BS 7671 Part 2?
flashcards.back: Protective conductor current: electric current appearing in a protective conductor, such as leakage current or current resulting from an insulation fault.
An overcurrent resulting from a fault of negligible impedance between live conductors having a difference in potential under normal operating conditions.

flashcards.front: What minimum IP rating must consumer unit external covers provide?
flashcards.back: At least IP4X, and all cable entry points must offer the same protection.

flashcards.front: What construction material is required for domestic consumer unit enclosures?
flashcards.back: Non-combustible material, or the unit must be enclosed in a non-combustible cabinet. Ferrous metal such as steel is an example.

quiz.q: Which device is normally used as the distributor's cut-out in a single phase supply?
quiz.why: The cut-out normally takes the form of a BS 88 cartridge fuse, commonly 80 A or 100 A.

quiz.q: After the cut-out fuse carrier is pulled out, which connection is still present?
quiz.why: Removal of the fuse only breaks the line connection; the neutral is still present.

quiz.q: What csa of meter tails is commonly installed for supplies up to 100 A?
quiz.why: 25 mm² tails are common because they have a current carrying capacity of 101 A (Reference Method B).

quiz.q: Why were 16 mm² tails commonly deemed sufficient in older installations?
options: They carry up to 87 A and an 80 A fuse was fitted
They are not protected by the cut-out
They are used only with RCDs
quiz.why: 16 mm² can carry up to 87 A (Reference Method C), which suited older installations with an 80 A fuse.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of the electricity isolator switch ahead of the consumer unit?
options: To isolate and lock off the main supply to the consumer unit
To protect against overload in each circuit
quiz.why: It allows the supply to the consumer unit to be isolated and locked off, for example when replacing the consumer unit.

quiz.q: Which term describes an overcurrent occurring in a circuit which is electrically sound?
quiz.why: Overload current occurs in an electrically sound circuit, caused by connected equipment.

quiz.q: Which term does BS 7671 Part 2 use for earth leakage current?
quiz.why: Earth leakage current is referred to as protective conductor current.

quiz.q: A short circuit is an overcurrent resulting from a fault of what kind?
quiz.why: The fault lies between live conductors and is of negligible impedance, zero Ω or very close to it.

quiz.q: In a consumer unit, which device protects against a fault before the circuit breakers?
quiz.why: Any overcurrent fault before the circuit breakers is protected by the 100 A distributor's cut-out.

quiz.q: What minimum protection must the external covers of a consumer unit provide?
quiz.why: External covers must provide protection of at least IP4X.

quiz.q: Which material is given as an example of non-combustible for consumer unit enclosures?
quiz.why: Ferrous metal, e.g. steel, is deemed to be a non-combustible material.
